title: Tight Entropy Contraction of Generalized Quantum Depolarization
abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for relative entropy contraction of generalized quantum depolarizing channels and semigroups. Our bound provides tight first order asymptotic of the contraction rate in terms of the dimension constant. One side estimate are based on sharp reverse ratio and convexity of relative entropy of two states, which can be derived from the recently introduced Hockey-Stick quantum $f$-divergence, and also independently, Bogoliubov--Kubo--Mori quantum Fisher information metric. The other side follows from the existence of index achieving pure state with respect to a general conditional expectation. Our results extend to the complete entropy contraction rate, tensor stable estimates for product dynamics. Examples include quantum depolarization, dephasing, and compact group symmetrization, with consequences for the decay rate of coherence and asymmetry.
summary: This theoretical paper develops sharp bounds for the rate at which quantum information decays under generalized noise processes. By analyzing the relative entropy contraction using advanced tools like quantum f-divergences, the authors provide asymptotic formulas for these decay rates. The results are crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum coherence preservation in noisy quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes tight upper and lower bounds for the relative entropy contraction rate of generalized quantum depolarizing channels and semigroups.
main_result: It derives asymptotic formulas for the contraction rates ($\alpha(P_E^t)$ and $\eta(\Phi_E^p)$) in terms of the structural constants $C(E)$ and $C_{cb}(E)$, and proves the tensor stability of these complete constants.
method: The analysis heavily relies on bounding ratios of relative entropies using tools like the Hockey-Stick quantum f-divergence and the Bogoliubov–Kubo–Mori quantum Fisher information metric.
model_or_system: The study analyzes quantum dynamics governed by generalized quantum depolarizing channels ($\Phi_E^p$) and semigroups ($P_E^t$), which are modeled using faithful conditional expectations ($E$). Examples include quantum depolarization and dephasing.
key_observables: Relative entropy $D(ho\|\sigma)$, complete contraction constants $C_{cb}(E)$, and the contraction rates $\alpha(P_E^t)$ and $\eta(\Phi_E^p)$.
important_parameters: The structural constants $C(E)$ and $C_{cb}(E)$, which quantify the noise strength and are crucial for determining the asymptotic decay rates.
main_assumptions: The derivation of the lower bound relies on the existence of an index-achieving pure state, and the final results are presented as asymptotic estimates for large structural constants.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing general bounds using relative entropy ratios (Chunk 2), then applying these tools to the specific dynamics of quantum depolarizing channels (Chunk 1), and finally deriving the asymptotic forms and proving the multiplicative properties of the complete index (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on how quantum information (coherence, entanglement) decays under realistic noise models, which is fundamental for designing fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.
